Very interesting! What happened:
- Player moved up 4 rows: white cap 40→36? No wait. Let me re-read.
Before (after SPACE): player white cap row 40, green rows 41–43, cols 32–35. Blue square at rows 37–38, cols 33–34.
After UP:
- Player: white cap now at row 36 (from diff, W appears at rows 32–35? No…). Let me parse the diff:
  - Rows 32–35, cols 32–35: 'w' → 'W', but (33,33),(33,34),(34,33),(34,34) became 'b'. So a new white frame (W) appeared at rows 32–35, cols 32–35, with a blue square inside at rows 33–34, cols 33–34!
  - Rows 37–39, cols 32–35: 'W'/'b' → 'N'. So the old blue square (rows 37–38) and the white area around it became green (N) — the player is now at rows 37–39!
  - Rows 40–43: W/N → w (the old player position is now empty).
So the player moved up 4 rows (from rows 41–43 to rows 37–39… wait, the player body is 3 rows: green rows 41,42,43 + white cap row 40. After moving: green rows 37,38,39 + white cap row 36). Yes, the player moved up 4 rows.
And the blue square at rows 37–38, cols 33–34 was "carried" by the player — it moved up together with the player! Now the blue square is at rows 33–34, cols 33–34, and a white frame (W) appeared around it at rows 32–35, cols 32–35.
So the mechanic is: when the player moves onto an exposed blue square, they pick it up and carry it. The carried blue square is displayed above the player's head with a white frame? Wait, the white frame is at rows 32–35, and the player's white cap is at row 36. Hmm, so the carried item is displayed as a blue square inside a white frame, positioned just above the player (adjacent to the player's white cap).
Actually wait — the player's white cap is at row 36 (cols 32–35), and the white frame (W) is at rows 32–35, cols 32–35, with the blue square inside it at rows 33–34. So the carried item is displayed directly above the player, as a white-framed box containing a blue square.
So the game is: collect blue squares (from opened boxes) and… carry them somewhere? Probably to the blue rectangle with the gray bar (rows 28–31, cols 28–39) — that might be the "drop zone"/goal! The gray bar inside the blue rectangle might be where the item is placed.
So the goal is probably: collect all 3 blue squares and drop them into the blue rectangle (the "bin"/"goal"). The gray bar might be a placeholder showing where the items go.
So next: the player is at rows 37–39, cols 32–35 (white cap row 36). The blue rectangle is at rows 28–31, cols 28–39. If the player moves up 4 rows, they'll be at rows 33–35 + cap row 32, still below the rectangle (rows 28–31). Move up once more: rows 29–31 + cap row 28 — that overlaps with the blue rectangle's rows! Maybe the player can't enter the rectangle (it's a wall), or maybe they can drop the item.
Hmm, wait, but the carried item is at rows 32–35 (above the player's cap). If the player moves up so the cap reaches row 28… the item would be at rows 24–27, above the rectangle. That doesn't seem right either.
Let me think differently. Maybe the white frame around the carried blue square is just how the "held item" is rendered: a small box above the player's head. When the player reaches the goal (the blue rectangle), they press SPACE to drop it.
Let me try moving up toward the blue rectangle and see what happens. The player's cap is at row 36. The rectangle is at rows 28–31. Move up once: player at rows 33–35, cap row 32. Move up again: player at rows 29–31, cap row 28 — overlaps with the rectangle's rows 28–31, cols 28–39 (player is cols 32–35, within the rectangle's cols 28–39). So the second UP might be blocked, or the player might enter the rectangle.
Let me test one UP at a time.
